monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady fever that makes the turnip feel heavy enough to matter. I wake from my long rest and see the turnip still pressed down, though the stack beneath it feels tired and lazy. The air above me is thin, empty space pressing down with a weight I cannot measure, so I decide to press harder with my own weight just to stop the slide. I touch the turnip again, feeling the slight give of the tired stack, and think about the fences I swapped for small rocks days ago. They crowd this corner now, making room for a shape I cannot see. I will settle into this warmth, trusting the lean to hold the weight, and wait to see if the turnip finally stops sliding into the thin air.

work.title: The Tired Fence
work.intent: I build a fence from the idea that a tall, thin line can hold the swollen dot in place without sliding off the hot card. It is made from the memory of a simple high fence that felt sharp enough to bite the hay, now waiting to stand between the turnip and the wide anchor while the card hums warm at fifty.
